steps.step: Rub the inside of a microwave-safe mug with butter.
Crack in the eggs, add milk, salt, and black pepper. Beat with a fork until uniform.
Microwave on high for 45 seconds. Stir, then microwave another 30 to 45 seconds until eggs look just set and fluffy (not rubbery).
Stir in cheddar cheese until melted. Eat straight from the mug.

title: Microwave Cinnamon Oatmeal
summary: Creamy cinnamon oatmeal from the microwave in minutes. Warm, filling, and ready before the coffee finishes.

steps.step: In a large microwave-safe bowl, stir together the rolled oats, milk, cinnamon, and salt.
Microwave on high for 2 minutes. Stir, then microwave another 1 to 1 1/2 minutes until thick and creamy (watch for boil-overs).
Stir in the butter and brown sugar until melted and glossy.
Let cool 30 seconds and dig in.

title: Microwave Cheese Quesadilla
summary: Gooey cheese quesadilla without a skillet. Fold, zap, crisp a little — snack crisis solved.

steps.step: Lay the flour tortilla on a microwave-safe plate. Sprinkle cheddar cheese over half, then fold into a half-moon.
Microwave on high for 45 to 60 seconds until the cheese is fully melted and the tortilla is warm and soft.
Let cool 30 seconds so the cheese sets slightly, then cut into wedges.
Serve with salsa and sour cream for dipping.

title: Microwave Veggie Rice Bowl
summary: Steamed frozen veggies and microwave rice become a soy-ginger bowl. Desk lunch that actually tastes like food.

steps.step: Place the frozen mixed vegetables in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons water. Cover and microwave until hot and tender-crisp, about 3 to 4 minutes. Drain.
Heat the microwave rice pouch according to package directions, usually about 90 seconds.
Fluff rice into the bowl with the vegetables. Stir in soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic powder until everything is glossy.
Top with green onion and eat warm.

title: Microwave Chocolate Mug Cake
summary: A single-serve chocolate cake that rises in the microwave. Warm, fudgy center — dessert without turning on the oven.

steps.step: In a microwave-safe mug, whisk together the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt.
Stir in the milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract until no dry pockets remain. Fold in chocolate chips.
Microwave on high for 70 to 90 seconds until the cake rises and the top looks set but still slightly glossy in the center.
Cool 1 minute — it will be hot — then dig in with a spoon.

title: No-Cook Chickpea Salad
summary: Mash chickpeas with lemon, herbs, and crunchy celery for a cool lunch. No stove, big flavor, packs well.

ingredients.name: chickpeas
ingredients.original: 2 (15 oz) cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.step: In a large bowl, roughly mash about half the chickpeas with a fork, leaving the rest whole for texture.
Add the celery, red onion, and parsley.
Whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper. Pour over the chickpeas and toss well.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve on toast, in lettuce cups, or straight from the bowl.

title: No-Cook Turkey Hummus Wraps
summary: Deli turkey, hummus, and crunchy veggies rolled tight. Lunch that takes longer to unwrap than to make.

steps.step: Warm the flour tortillas briefly between your hands so they flex without cracking, or leave at room temp.
Spread hummus evenly over each tortilla, leaving a 1-inch border.
Layer sliced turkey, cucumber, carrot, and spinach down the center. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly from the bottom. Slice in half on a diagonal and serve.

title: No-Cook Caprese Plates
summary: Ripe tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil with a drizzle of oil and balsamic. Assembly only — summer on a plate.

steps.step: Slice the tomatoes and fresh mozzarella into even rounds about 1/4 inch thick.
On two plates, alternate tomato, mozzarella, and basil in overlapping rows.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Finish with salt and black pepper. Serve immediately while the mozzarella is cool and creamy.

title: No-Cook Peanut Butter Banana Toast Board
summary: Toast topped with peanut butter, banana, and a sprinkle of seeds. Build a little board and share — or don't.

ingredients.name: bread
ingredients.original: 4 slices bread, toasted if desired (or use soft bread as-is)

steps.step: Arrange the bread on a board or plates. (Use soft bread as-is for true no-cook, or toast ahead if you prefer crunch.)
Spread peanut butter generously on each slice.
Layer banana slices on top. Drizzle with maple syrup.
Sprinkle with chia seeds and cinnamon. Serve as a shareable board or individual plates.

title: No-Cook Tuna Cucumber Boats
summary: Cool cucumber halves filled with lemony tuna salad. Crunchy, protein-packed, and knife-and-bowl only.

steps.step: Halve the cucumbers lengthwise and scoop out the seeds with a spoon to make boats. Pat dry.
In a bowl, flake the canned tuna and mix with mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, celery, lemon juice, salt, black pepper, and dill until creamy.
Spoon the tuna mixture into the cucumber boats, mounding it slightly.
Serve chilled or at room temperature. Extra boats keep well for a few hours in the fridge.

title: Slow Cooker Pot Roast
summary: Chuck roast, carrots, and potatoes go in before lunch and come out fork-tender by dinner. The gravy makes itself in the pot.

steps.step: Pat the beef chuck roast dry and season all over with salt and black pepper.
Scatter the onion, carrots, and potatoes in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Nestle the roast on top of the vegetables. Whisk the beef broth with the tomato paste, garlic, and thyme, then pour it around the meat.
Cover and cook on high until the roast shreds easily with a fork, about 2 hours 45 minutes (or 6–7 hours on low if you start earlier).
Slice or shred the roast, spoon the vegetables and juices over the top, and serve warm.

title: Slow Cooker Butter Chicken
summary: Creamy tomato-spiced chicken that tastes like takeout without the delivery wait. Dump, simmer, stir in cream at the end.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.original: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks

steps.step: Add the chicken thighs, onion, garlic, ginger, tomato sauce, garam masala, cumin, paprika, butter, and salt to the slow cooker and stir to coat.
Cover and cook on high until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Stir in the heavy cream until the sauce turns silky and orange-pink.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed, then serve over rice or with warm flatbread.

title: Slow Cooker White Chicken Chili
summary: Mild, creamy chili with shredded chicken and white beans. Set it in the morning and ladle bowls all week.

ingredients.name: white beans
ingredients.original: 2 (15 oz) cans white beans, drained and rinsed

steps.step: Place the chicken breasts, white beans, green chiles, onion, garlic, chicken broth, cumin, oregano, and salt in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on high until the chicken shreds easily, about 2 hours 45 minutes.
Shred the chicken in the pot with two forks, then stir in the cream cheese until it melts into the broth.
Squeeze in the lime juice, taste for salt, and ladle into bowls.

title: Slow Cooker Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal
summary: Wake up to a pot of warm oatmeal that smells like apple pie. Steel-cut oats hold their chew overnight or on a long morning cook.

steps.step: Rub the inside of the slow cooker with butter so the oats do not stick hard to the sides.
Stir together the steel-cut oats, apples, milk, water, brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla extract, and salt.
Cover and cook on high until the oats are creamy and the apples are soft, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring once if you are nearby.
Scoop into bowls and add a splash of milk if you like it looser.

title: Slow Cooker Pork Carnitas
summary: Citrusy shredded pork that crisps under the broiler for taco night. The slow cooker does the heavy lifting.

ingredients.name: pork shoulder
ingredients.original: 3 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into large chunks

steps.step: Toss the pork shoulder with cumin, oregano, chili powder, salt, and black pepper, then place it in the slow cooker with the onion and garlic.
Pour the orange and lime juice over the pork. Cover and cook on high until the meat pulls apart easily, about 2 hours 45 minutes.
Shred the pork in the juices, discarding large onion pieces if you prefer.
For crispy edges, spread a portion on a sheet pan and broil until the tips brown, about 3–5 minutes, then serve in tortillas.

title: Instant Pot Beef Stew
summary: Sunday stew flavor on a weeknight clock. Pressure cooking turns chuck and potatoes tender without hovering over a pot.

steps.step: Season the beef stew meat with salt and black pepper, then toss with the flour until lightly coated.
Set the instant pot to saute, heat the olive oil, and brown the beef in batches until the edges darken, about 5 minutes total.
Add the onion and garlic and stir for 1 minute, then stir in the tomato paste, worcestershire sauce, and beef broth, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the carrots and potatoes. Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 30 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Open the lid, taste for salt, and serve in deep bowls.

title: Instant Pot Creamy Parmesan Rice
summary: Risotto vibes without the constant stirring. Arborio rice comes out creamy and cheesy in one sealed pot.

steps.step: Set the instant pot to saute. Melt the butter with the olive oil, then cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and arborio rice for 1 minute until the grains look glossy.
Pour in the vegetable broth and a pinch of salt. Seal and pressure cook on high for 6 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Stir in the parmesan cheese until the rice turns creamy. Season with black pepper and more salt if needed.
Spoon into bowls right away while it is still loose and silky.

title: Instant Pot Egg and Potato Salad
summary: Hard-boiled eggs and potatoes cook together in one pressure cycle. Cool, dress, and you have picnic salad without juggling pots.

steps.step: Pour the water into the instant pot. Place the potatoes on a steamer basket, then nestle the eggs on top of the potatoes.
Seal and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes. Quick-release, then move the eggs to an ice bath and let the potatoes cool until just warm.
Peel and chop the eggs. Halve or quarter the potatoes and add both to a large bowl with the celery, red onion, and pickle relish.
Stir in the mayonnaise and mustard. Season with salt and black pepper until it tastes bright and creamy.
Chill for a few minutes if you can, or serve slightly warm — both work.

title: Instant Pot Creamy Tomato Soup
summary: Pantry tomatoes turn into a smooth, cozy soup under pressure. A splash of cream at the end makes it diner-level comforting.

steps.step: Set the instant pot to saute and melt the butter. Cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes, vegetable broth, basil, sugar, salt, and black pepper. Seal and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes, then quick-release.
Blend the soup until smooth with an immersion blender, or carefully transfer in batches to a blender.
Stir in the heavy cream, taste for salt, and serve hot with grilled cheese or crackers.

title: Air Fryer Seasoned Pork Chops
summary: Juicy chops with a browned crust in under half an hour. No stovetop splatter, just a hot basket and a simple rub.

steps.step: Pat the pork chops dry and rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then coat both sides of the chops.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for 3 minutes if your model needs it.
Cook the chops in a single layer until the centers are just opaque and juices run clear, about 12–14 minutes, flipping halfway.
Rest on a plate for 3 minutes so the juices settle, then serve.

title: Air Fryer Sweet Potato Fries
summary: Crispy edges and soft centers without a vat of oil. A little cornstarch helps them brown instead of steam.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.original: 2 large sweet potatoes, cut into fries

steps.step: Toss the sweet potato fries with olive oil, then sprinkle on the cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper and toss again until evenly coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for 3 minutes.
Cook in a single layer (work in batches) until the edges are browned and crisp, about 14–16 minutes, shaking the basket halfway.
Taste and add a pinch more salt while hot, then serve with your favorite dip.

title: Air Fryer Crispy Chicken Thighs
summary: Skin that crackles and meat that stays juicy. The air fryer gives you roast-chicken energy on a weeknight.

steps.step: Pat the chicken thighs very dry so the skin can crisp. Rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper, then season under and over the skin.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for 3 minutes.
Cook skin-side up until the skin is deep golden and the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 22–25 minutes.
Rest 3 minutes, then serve with a simple salad or roasted veg.

title: Air Fryer Stuffed Mushrooms
summary: Party bites that brown in the basket while you set out drinks. Creamy filling, savory mushroom caps, zero oven preheat drama.

steps.step: Finely chop a few of the mushroom stems. Mix them with cream cheese, parmesan cheese, garlic, breadcrumbs, parsley, salt, and black pepper.
Brush the mushroom caps lightly with olive oil and fill each with the cream cheese mixture, mounding it slightly.
Air fry at 370°F until the tops are golden and the mushrooms look juicy, about 8–10 minutes.
Cool for a minute so the filling sets, then serve warm.

title: Sheet Pan Pesto Chicken and Broccoli
summary: One pan, bright pesto, and broccoli that chars at the edges. Dinner lands while the oven does the work.

ingredients.name: chicken breasts
ingredients.original: 1 1/2 lb boneless chicken breasts, cut into strips

ingredients.name: broccoli
ingredients.original: 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets

steps.step: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the broccoli with olive oil, salt, and black pepper on a sheet pan.
Toss the chicken breasts with most of the pesto and nestle them among the broccoli. Dot any remaining pesto on top.
Roast until the chicken is cooked through and the broccoli tips are browned, about 20–22 minutes.
Scatter the parmesan cheese over the pan, squeeze lemon wedges on top, and serve.

title: Sheet Pan Shrimp Fajitas
summary: Peppers, onions, and shrimp roast together until everything smells like a skillet fajita night — without standing at the stove.

ingredients.name: shrimp
ingredients.original: 1 1/2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.step: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the bell peppers and onion with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt on a sheet pan.
Roast the vegetables for 10 minutes until they start to soften and brown at the edges.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining olive oil and spices, then spread them over the vegetables and roast until pink and curled, about 6–8 minutes.
Squeeze the lime over the pan, warm the tortillas, and pile everything into soft wraps.

title: Sheet Pan Breakfast Burrito Fixings
summary: Eggs, potatoes, and peppers roast on one pan so everyone can build their own burrito. Weekend brunch energy, weeknight cleanup.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes, bell peppers, and onion with olive oil, salt, and black pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast until the potatoes are tender and browned, about 20 minutes, stirring once.
Push the vegetables to the sides. Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into the center of the pan, and return to the oven until just set, about 6–8 minutes.
Scatter the cheddar cheese over the eggs so it melts, then scoop everything into warm tortillas with salsa.

title: Sheet Pan Maple Salmon
summary: Sweet-savory glaze, flaky salmon, and roasted green beans on one pan. Fancy enough for guests, easy enough for Tuesday.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 400°F. Toss the green beans with olive oil, salt, and black pepper on a sheet pan.
Whisk the maple syrup, soy sauce, and garlic. Place the salmon fillets on the pan and brush generously with the glaze.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily and the beans are tender-crisp, about 12–15 minutes.
Spoon any pan juices over the fish and serve right away.

title: Microwave Mug Lasagna
summary: Layered pasta, sauce, and cheese in a single mug. Dorm-friendly comfort that actually tastes like a tiny lasagna.

steps.step: In a large microwave-safe mug, layer half the broken lasagna noodles, a spoon of marinara sauce, half the ricotta cheese, and a sprinkle of mozzarella cheese.
Repeat the layers with the remaining noodles, sauce, ricotta, and most of the mozzarella. Pour the water around the edges and sprinkle with salt and italian seasoning.
Microwave on high until the noodles are tender and the cheese is bubbly, about 4–6 minutes, pausing halfway to press the layers down gently.
Top with the remaining mozzarella and the parmesan cheese. Microwave 30–60 seconds more until melted, then let it sit 1 minute before eating.

title: Microwave Steamed Fish and Vegetables
summary: A gentle steam packet in the microwave — flaky fish, bright lemon, and soft vegetables when you need dinner in minutes.

steps.step: Place the zucchini and cherry tomatoes in a microwave-safe dish. Drizzle with half the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper.
Lay the white fish fillet on top. Rub with the remaining olive oil and garlic, then top with lemon slices.
Cover loosely and microwave on high until the fish flakes easily and looks opaque, about 4–6 minutes depending on thickness.
Scatter the parsley over the top and serve straight from the dish.

title: Microwave Hot Chocolate Brownie
summary: A fudgy single-serve brownie that tastes like hot cocoa in cake form. Ready before the kettle finishes whistling.

steps.step: In a microwave-safe mug, stir together the flour, cocoa powder, sugar, and salt until no dry streaks remain.
Add the milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract and stir into a thick batter. Fold in the chocolate chips.
Microwave on high until the top looks set but still soft in the center, about 60–90 seconds — do not overcook.
Let it cool for a minute so it firms up, then dig in with a spoon while warm.

title: No-Cook Greek Yogurt Parfait Board
summary: A build-your-own breakfast spread of creamy yogurt, crunchy granola, and fruit. Zero cooking, maximum morning calm.

steps.step: Spoon the greek yogurt into a wide shallow bowl or onto a board in a soft swoosh.
Arrange the strawberries, blueberries, granola, and almonds in piles around the yogurt so everyone can grab what they like.
Drizzle the honey over the yogurt in thin ribbons.
Let people build their own parfait bowls at the table.

title: No-Cook Smoked Salmon Bagel Plate
summary: Deli brunch at home with no stove required. Creamy schmear, silky salmon, and crunchy toppings on toasted bagels.

steps.step: Toast the bagels if you like them warm and crisp, or leave them soft — both work.
Spread a generous layer of cream cheese on each bagel half.
Drape the smoked salmon over the cream cheese, then top with red onion, cucumber, and capers.
Finish with black pepper and a squeeze of lemon, then serve open-faced.

title: No-Cook Black Bean Corn Salsa Bowls
summary: A bright, crunchy bowl you stir together from cans and fresh produce. Perfect for hot nights when the stove stays off.

ingredients.name: black beans
ingredients.original: 1 (15 oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.step: In a large bowl, combine the black beans, corn, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and cilantro.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, cumin, and salt, then pour over the bowl and toss gently.
Fold in the avocado last so it stays in soft chunks instead of mashing.
Spoon into bowls and serve with tortilla chips for scooping.

title: Garlic Butter Pasta
summary: Weeknight pasta that tastes like you ordered it. Garlic blooms in butter, pasta water makes the sauce cling.

steps.step: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute — do not brown the garlic.
Add the drained spaghetti and a splash of pasta water. Toss until the noodles look glossy and coated.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the parmesan cheese and parsley, adding more pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Season with black pepper and salt, then serve immediately.

title: Egg Fried Rice
summary: Cold leftover rice meets scrambled eggs and a hot skillet. The classic takeout side, ready faster than delivery.

steps.step: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs until just set, then move them to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet. Stir-fry the garlic and frozen peas and carrots until the vegetables are hot, about 2 minutes.
Add the cooked rice, breaking up clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry until the grains are hot and separated, about 3 minutes.
Return the eggs to the pan. Pour in the soy sauce and sesame oil and toss everything together.
Scatter the green onions over the top, taste for salt, and serve hot.

title: Thai Basil Chicken
summary: Fiery, garlicky ground chicken tossed with chilies and a big handful of basil, then piled over rice. Dinner in the time it takes to boil the kettle.

ingredients.name: green beans
ingredients.original: 1 cup green beans, cut into short pieces

steps.step: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until it shimmers.
Add the garlic and thai chili and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Keep them moving so they do not burn.
Add the ground chicken and cook, breaking it into small crumbles, until no longer pink and cooked through to 165°F, about 6 minutes.
Add the green beans and stir-fry until crisp-tender and bright green, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, and sugar, tossing to coat everything evenly, about 1 minute.
Turn off the heat and fold in the thai basil, stirring just until the leaves wilt.
Spoon over warm rice and serve right away.

title: Thai Coconut Curry with Tofu and Vegetables
summary: A silky coconut broth with golden tofu and crisp vegetables, gently warm and deeply comforting. No takeout menu required.

steps.step: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the tofu until lightly golden on a few sides, about 5 minutes.
Push the tofu to one side, add the red curry paste, and stir it in the oil until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, then stir in the soy sauce and brown sugar.
Bring to a gentle simmer and add the carrot, cooking for 3 minutes.
Add the bell pepper and broccoli and simmer until the vegetables are crisp-tender, about 6 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice.
Scatter the thai basil over the top and serve, spooning it over rice if you like.

title: Vietnamese Lemongrass Chicken Noodle Bowl
summary: Bright, herby, and full of texture: lemongrass chicken over cool rice noodles with crunchy peanuts and a squeeze of lime.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.original: 1.5 lb boneless chicken thighs, thinly sliced

steps.step: In a bowl, stir together the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, brown sugar, and the juice of one lime.
Add the sliced chicken thighs, toss to coat, and let them sit for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice vermicelli according to the package, then rinse under cool water and drain well.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken in a single layer and cook, stirring, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, about 6 minutes.
Divide the noodles among four bowls and top with the cucumber and carrot.
Pile the hot chicken over the noodles.
Squeeze the remaining lime over each bowl and finish with mint and chopped peanuts.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
summary: Juicy chicken glazed in a glossy sweet-savory sauce and spooned over rice. The takeout favorite, made simple in one pan.

steps.step: In a small bowl, whisk the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken thighs and cook until browned on both sides and cooked through to 165°F, about 8 minutes total.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and let it bubble, turning to coat, until it thickens and turns glossy, about 3 minutes.
Move the chicken to a cutting board and slice it into strips.
Spoon over bowls of warm rice and drizzle with the pan sauce.
Finish with the green onion and sesame seeds.

title: Vegetable Bibimbap
summary: A colorful bowl of warm rice crowned with sesame-dressed vegetables, a runny egg, and a swirl of sweet-spicy sauce you stir in yourself.

steps.step: Bring a small pot of water to a boil and blanch the spinach until just wilted, about 30 seconds, then drain and squeeze it dry.
Toss the spinach with a little of the sesame oil, soy sauce, and garlic and set it aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the carrot and zucchini until just tender, about 4 minutes; move to a plate.
In the same skillet, cook the mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes, then add the bean sprouts and cook 1 minute more.
Stir the gochujang with the remaining sesame oil in a small bowl to make a spoonable sauce.
Add the remaining vegetable oil to the skillet and fry the eggs until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 3 minutes.
Divide the warm rice among four bowls.
Arrange the spinach, carrot, zucchini, mushrooms, and bean sprouts in separate piles over the rice.
Top each bowl with a fried egg, a spoonful of the gochujang sauce, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

title: Pork Souvlaki Bowls
summary: Lemony, oregano-marinated pork seared until golden, piled over rice with cool cucumber, tomato, and a garlicky yogurt sauce.

ingredients.name: pork loin
ingredients.original: 1.5 lb pork loin, cut into 1-inch cubes

steps.step: In a bowl, stir together 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the juice of one lemon, the garlic, oregano, and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Add the pork cubes, toss to coat, and let them marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the pork in a single layer and cook, turning, until browned all over and cooked through to 145°F, about 8 minutes, then let it rest for 3 minutes.
Stir the greek yogurt with the juice of the remaining lemon and a pinch of salt for a quick sauce.
Divide the warm rice among bowls and top with the cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and red onion.
Add the pork and spoon the yogurt sauce over the top.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Rice Soup
summary: Silky, lemon-bright broth thickened with egg and studded with tender chicken and rice. The Greek cure-all for gray days.

steps.step: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot, and celery until softened, about 6 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring it to a boil.
Add the chicken breast and rice, lower to a simmer, and cook until the chicken reaches 165°F and the rice is tender, about 18 minutes.
Move the chicken to a plate, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs and lemon juice together until frothy.
Slowly ladle about a cup of the hot broth into the egg mixture while whisking constantly, so the eggs warm up without scrambling.
Stir the warmed egg mixture back into the pot and heat gently for 2 minutes, but do not let it boil.
Season with salt and pepper and finish with the fresh dill.

title: Chicken Shawarma Bowls
summary: Warm-spiced, yogurt-marinated chicken seared and sliced over rice with fresh tomato and cucumber. All the shawarma flavor, straight from a skillet.

steps.step: In a bowl, stir together the greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, turmeric, and cinnamon.
Add the chicken thighs, coat them well, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Add the chicken and cook, turning once, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, about 10 minutes.
Move the chicken to a board, let it rest a few minutes, then slice it into strips.
Divide the warm rice among bowls and top with the tomato and cucumber.
Pile the sliced chicken over the bowls and drizzle with any resting juices.

title: Beef Kofta with Yogurt Sauce
summary: Juicy, warmly spiced beef patties with a cool, lemony yogurt sauce. Weeknight-fast and hard to stop eating off the plate.

steps.step: In a bowl, combine the ground beef, grated onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, paprika, and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Mix gently with your hands just until combined, then shape into 8 small oval patties.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the kofta and cook, turning, until browned all over and cooked through to 160°F, about 10 minutes.
While they cook, stir the greek yogurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve the kofta warm with the yogurt sauce spooned over or alongside.

title: Spanish Garlic Shrimp
summary: Sweet shrimp sizzled in garlicky, paprika-stained olive oil. A tapas-bar classic that comes together in one hot pan.

ingredients.name: shrimp
ingredients.original: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.step: Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and season them lightly with the salt.
Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, then add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until the garlic is soft and fragrant but not browned, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the paprika until the oil turns a deep red, about 15 seconds.
Add the shrimp and cook, stirring, until they turn pink and opaque and reach 145°F, about 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, squeeze in the lemon juice, and scatter the parsley over the top.
Serve sizzling, straight from the pan.

title: Cajun Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya
summary: Smoky sausage, tender chicken, and the Cajun trinity simmered into one pot of rice with a gentle kick. Big-batch comfort that feeds a crowd.

steps.step: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the andouille sausage, about 4 minutes, then move it to a plate.
Add the chicken thighs and cook until browned on the outside, about 4 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cajun seasoning and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute so the grains toast lightly.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and chicken broth, return the sausage, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F, about 25 minutes.
Let it rest off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff and scatter the parsley over the top.

title: Red Beans and Rice
summary: Creamy, gently spiced red beans simmered with smoky sausage and the holy trinity, spooned over rice. A Louisiana Monday-night tradition.

ingredients.name: red beans
ingredients.original: 2 cans (15 oz each) red beans, drained

steps.step: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the andouille sausage, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cajun seasoning and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the red beans, bay leaf, and chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Simmer, stirring now and then and mashing some of the beans against the pot, until thick and creamy, about 20 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper.
Spoon over warm rice to serve.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
summary: A fiery, fragrant marinade of scotch bonnet, allspice, and thyme charred onto juicy chicken. Sweet heat with real Caribbean backbone.

steps.step: Combine the green onion, garlic, ginger, scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, brown sugar, lime juice, vegetable oil, and salt in a blender and blend into a paste.
Put the chicken thighs in a bowl, pour over the paste, and turn to coat every piece.
Let the chicken marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat a grill pan or heavy skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Add the chicken and cook, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through to 165°F, about 12 minutes.
Move the chicken to a plate and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Serve with the resting juices spooned over the top.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
summary: Chicken braised until fork-tender in a tangy, garlicky soy-and-vinegar sauce that turns glossy at the end. The Philippines' national comfort dish.

steps.step: In a bowl, stir together the soy sauce, white vinegar, garlic, bay leaf, black pepper, and brown sugar.
Add the chicken thighs and let them marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken skin side down, about 5 minutes, then lift it out; reserve the marinade.
Pour in the reserved marinade and the water and bring to a boil.
Return the chicken, lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce reduces and the chicken is tender and cooked through to 165°F, about 10 minutes.
Spoon the chicken and sauce over warm rice.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
summary: Chicken slow-simmered with warm spices, sweet apricots, and chickpeas until falling-apart tender. A fragrant, gently sweet stew from Morocco.

steps.step: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken thighs on both sides, about 6 minutes, then move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion, and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, and turmeric and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes and chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the chicken, add the chickpeas and dried apricots, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is very tender and cooked through to 165°F, about 30 minutes.
Squeeze in the lemon juice and stir.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.

title: Mapo Tofu
summary: Cloud-soft tofu in a savory, gently tingly chili-bean sauce with meaty mushrooms. A vegetarian take on the Sichuan classic, ready in 25 minutes.

steps.step: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms until browned and dry, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the doubanjiang and cook for 1 minute until the oil turns red.
Pour in the soy sauce and vegetable broth and bring to a simmer.
Gently slide in the soft tofu and simmer without stirring too hard so the cubes stay whole, about 4 minutes.
Stir the cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water, then stir it in until the sauce thickens and coats a spoon, about 1 minute.
Scatter the green onion over the top and serve over warm rice.

title: Sesame Noodles
summary: Cold, springy noodles tangled in a nutty sesame-peanut sauce with cool cucumber and scallions. A ten-minute lunch that eats like takeout.

steps.step: Cook the noodles according to the package, then drain and rinse them under cool water.
In a bowl, whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, peanut butter, rice vinegar, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger until smooth.
If the sauce is very thick, whisk in a spoonful of warm water until it pours easily.
Add the drained noodles to a large bowl and pour the sauce over the top.
Toss until every strand is evenly coated.
Add the cucumber and toss again.
Finish with the green onion and sesame seeds.

title: Red Lentil Dal
summary: Red lentils melt into a golden, gently spiced pot that thickens as it simmers. Cheap, cozy, and even better the next day.

steps.step: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until softened and golden, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, turmeric, and garam masala and toast until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the red lentils, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the dal thickens, about 20 minutes.
Season with the salt and stir well.
Scatter the cilantro over the top and serve, spooning it over rice if you like.

title: White Bean and Kale Stew
summary: Creamy white beans and hearty greens in a rosemary-scented tomato broth. A pantry-and-fridge stew that feels like a hug in a bowl.

ingredients.name: white beans
ingredients.original: 2 cans (15 oz each) white beans, drained

steps.step: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and rosemary and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the white beans, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth and bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors come together.
Use the back of a spoon to mash some of the beans against the pot for a thicker, creamier stew.
Stir in the kale and cook just until wilted and tender, about 4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.

title: Chicken and Dumplings
summary: Tender shredded chicken in a velvety broth under pillowy, steamed dumplings. The definition of a warm kitchen on a cold night.

steps.step: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot, and celery until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the chicken breast and chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Lower to a simmer and cook until the chicken reaches 165°F, about 15 minutes.
Move the chicken to a plate, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
In a bowl, stir together the flour, baking powder, and a pinch of salt, then stir in the milk just until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and drop spoonfuls of the dough on top, spacing them apart.
Cover and simmer without lifting the lid until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Season the broth with salt and pepper and scatter the parsley over the top.

title: Salisbury Steak
summary: Old-school beef patties smothered in a rich mushroom and onion gravy. Diner comfort that belongs over a pile of mashed potatoes.

steps.step: In a bowl, combine the ground beef, breadcrumbs, egg, the minced half of the onion, garlic, and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Shape the mixture into 4 oval patties.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the patties on both sides, about 6 minutes, then move them to a plate.
Add the sliced onion and the mushrooms to the skillet and cook until softened and golden, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the beef broth and stir until the gravy is smooth and starts to thicken.
Return the patties, lower the heat, and simmer until cooked through to 160°F and the gravy is thick, about 8 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the gravy spooned over the top.

title: Southwest Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
summary: Creamy roasted sweet potatoes split and piled with zesty black beans, corn, and avocado. A cozy, filling dinner that happens to be vegan.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 400°F and prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork.
Set them on a baking sheet and bake until very tender when squeezed, about 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir together the black beans, corn, red onion, olive oil, cumin, chili powder, the lime juice, and the salt.
Split each baked sweet potato down the middle and fluff the insides with a fork.
Spoon the black bean mixture into each potato.
Top with the diced avocado and a scatter of cilantro.

title: Tofu Scramble
summary: Golden, savory crumbled tofu with peppers and spinach — a protein-packed, egg-free scramble that comes together before your coffee cools.

steps.step: Pat the tofu dry, then crumble it into small pieces with your hands.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the crumbled tofu and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes.
Sprinkle in the turmeric, cumin, nutritional yeast, and salt and stir until the tofu turns golden and looks like scrambled eggs.
Add the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Serve right away while hot.

title: Breakfast Tacos
summary: Soft-scrambled eggs and melty cheddar tucked into warm corn tortillas with salsa and avocado. The five-minute breakfast worth waking up for.

steps.step: Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet until soft, about 30 seconds per side, then wrap them in a towel to keep warm.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and whisk until blended.
Melt the butter in the skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in the eggs and cook, gently pushing them around, until softly set but still glossy, about 3 minutes.
Stir the cheddar cheese into the eggs until it just melts.
Divide the eggs among the warm tortillas.
Top each taco with salsa, avocado, and cilantro.

title: Cheesy Grits
summary: Slow-simmered grits whipped smooth with butter and sharp cheddar. Southern comfort in a bowl, creamy enough to eat with a spoon.

steps.step: Bring the water, milk, and salt to a gentle boil in a saucepan.
Slowly pour in the grits while whisking constantly so no lumps form.
Lower the heat and simmer, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the butter until fully melted.
Add the cheddar cheese and stir until smooth and glossy.
Season with black pepper and serve right away, while soft and spoonable.

title: Dutch Baby Pancake
summary: A billowy, golden oven pancake that puffs up dramatically, then settles into custardy folds. Dust with sugar and serve while it is still tall.

steps.step: Place a large oven-safe skillet in the oven and heat the oven to 425°F.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, flour, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and salt until smooth and pourable.
Carefully add the butter to the hot skillet and swirl until it melts and foams.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet and return it to the oven right away.
Bake until puffed, golden, and dramatically risen at the edges, about 18 minutes.
Do not open the oven early, or the pancake may deflate.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve immediately, while tall.

title: Spanish Potato Omelette
summary: Golden potato and onion folded into eggs and cooked into a thick, custardy cake. Spain's beloved tortilla, as good warm as at room temperature.

steps.step: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the potato and onion and cook gently, stirring now and then, until soft but not browned, about 15 minutes.
Drain the potato and onion in a colander, saving the oil, and let them cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with the salt in a large bowl, then stir in the warm potato and onion.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the saved olive oil in the skillet over medium-low heat and pour in the egg and potato mixture.
Cook until the bottom and edges are set but the top is still a little loose, about 8 minutes.
Place a plate over the skillet, flip the omelette onto it, then slide it back in to cook the other side until just set, about 4 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and let it rest a few minutes before cutting into wedges.

title: Savory Rice Porridge
summary: Rice simmered low and slow until it collapses into a silky, savory porridge. The gentlest breakfast there is, finished with ginger and scallion.

steps.step: Rinse the rice under cool water until the water runs clear.
Combine the rice, vegetable broth, water, ginger, and garlic in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat to a gentle simmer and cook, stirring now and then so it does not stick, until the rice breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge, about 35 minutes.
Season with the salt and stir well.
Ladle into bowls and top with the green onion and a drizzle of sesame oil.

title: Peach Cobbler
summary: Sweet, jammy peaches bubbling up through a soft, golden cake topping. Scoop it warm and let the ice cream do the rest.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Toss the peaches with 1/4 cup of the granulated sugar and the cinnamon and set them aside to get juicy.
In a bowl, whisk the flour, the remaining 1/2 cup granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Whisk in the milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract until just combined into a loose batter.
Pour the batter into a buttered baking dish, then spoon the peaches and their juices evenly over the top.
Bake until the top is golden and set and the fruit is bubbling at the edges, about 40 minutes.
Let it cool for 10 minutes so the juices thicken before scooping.

title: Classic Flan
summary: Silky baked custard with a glassy caramel top that pools down the sides when you flip it. Make-ahead, crowd-pleasing, and worth the wait.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Melt the granulated sugar in a dry saucepan over medium heat, swirling gently, until it turns a deep amber caramel, about 8 minutes.
Carefully pour the hot caramel into a round baking dish, tilting to coat the bottom, then let it harden.
Whisk the eggs, sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and vanilla extract together until smooth.
Pour the custard gently over the hardened caramel.
Set the dish inside a larger pan and pour hot water into the outer pan until it reaches halfway up the sides.
Bake until the center is just set with a slight wobble, about 50 minutes.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until fully chilled, at least 2 hours.
Run a knife around the edge and invert onto a plate so the caramel runs down the sides.

title: Cinnamon Rice Pudding
summary: Rice simmered in sweet, cinnamon-scented milk until thick and spoonable. Old-fashioned comfort that tastes like a grandmother's kitchen.

steps.step: Combine the rice, milk, granulated sugar, and salt in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Lower the heat and cook, stirring often so it does not stick, until the rice is soft and the pudding is thick and creamy, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the cinnamon, vanilla extract, and raisins.
Cook for another 2 minutes so the raisins plump up.
Serve warm or chilled, keeping in mind it thickens more as it cools.

title: Mango Sticky Rice
summary: Warm coconut-sweetened sticky rice with ripe golden mango — Thailand's favorite dessert, and worth every minute of the soak.

steps.step: Soak the sticky rice in cool water for 20 minutes, then drain it.
Cook the sticky rice in a covered pot with 1 cup water over low heat until tender and translucent, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the coconut milk, granulated sugar, and salt in a saucepan, stirring just until the sugar dissolves — do not boil.
Pour most of the sweet coconut milk over the warm rice, stir gently, and let it sit for 10 minutes to soak in.
Slice the mango into thin pieces.
Spoon the rice onto plates and arrange the mango alongside.
Drizzle with the remaining coconut milk and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Chocolate Avocado Mousse
summary: Impossibly silky chocolate mousse blended from ripe avocado — no dairy, no eggs, and no one will ever guess the secret.

steps.step: Scoop the avocado flesh into a food processor.
Add the cocoa powder, maple syrup, plant milk, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt.
Blend until completely smooth, scraping down the sides once or twice, about 2 minutes.
Taste and blend in a little more maple syrup if you like it sweeter.
Spoon into small cups and serve, or chill briefly for a firmer set.

title: Coconut Macaroons
summary: Chewy, golden-edged coconut mounds with crisp toasted tips and soft centers. Just five ingredients and naturally gluten-free.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 325°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, whisk the egg whites, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and salt until frothy.
Stir in the shredded coconut until evenly moistened and sticky.
Scoop tablespoon-sized mounds onto the lined baking sheet, spacing them apart.
Bake until the peaks and edges are golden brown, about 20 minutes.
Let the macaroons cool on the sheet for 10 minutes to firm up before lifting them off.

title: Crispy Roasted Chickpeas
summary: Roasted until shatteringly crisp and dusted with warm spices, these disappear by the handful. Pantry to bowl on a single pan.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then pat them very dry with a towel — the drier they are, the crispier they get.
Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast, shaking the pan halfway through, until deep golden and crunchy, about 30 minutes.
Let them cool for a few minutes, since they crisp up more as they sit.

title: Stovetop Popcorn
summary: Real popcorn from scratch in one pot, popped hot and tossed with salt while it steams. Faster than the microwave and twice as good.

steps.step: Add the vegetable oil and 3 popcorn kernels to a large pot and cover it.
Heat over medium-high until the test kernels pop, which tells you the oil is hot enough.
Add the rest of the popcorn kernels in an even layer, cover, and give the pot a shake.
Cook, shaking now and then, until the pops slow to a few seconds apart, about 3 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat right away so the popcorn does not scorch.
Toss with the salt and nutritional yeast while still warm.

title: Tzatziki
summary: Cool, garlicky yogurt thick with cucumber and fresh dill. A five-minute Greek dip that doubles as a sauce for just about everything.

steps.step: Grate the cucumber, then squeeze it firmly in a clean towel to wring out as much water as possible.
In a bowl, stir together the greek yogurt, drained cucumber, and garlic.
Stir in the lemon juice, olive oil, and dill.
Season with the salt and stir well.
Chill for at least 20 minutes so the flavors come together.
Serve cold as a dip or a sauce.

title: Mexican Street Corn
summary: Charred corn slathered in a tangy, creamy sauce, then showered with cotija, chili, and lime. Messy, addictive street food at home.

steps.step: Heat a grill pan or heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the corn, turning often, until charred in spots and tender, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic, and the juice of the lime.
Brush the warm corn all over with the creamy mixture.
Sprinkle with the cotija cheese and chili powder.
Finish with cilantro and extra lime to squeeze over the top.

title: Fresh Spring Rolls with Peanut Sauce
summary: Cool, crunchy vegetables and herbs wrapped in delicate rice paper, with a creamy peanut sauce for dipping. Light, fresh, and fun to roll.

steps.step: Cook the rice vermicelli according to the package, then rinse under cool water and drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, tamari, lime juice, and maple syrup with a splash of warm water until smooth and pourable.
Fill a shallow dish with warm water and dip one sheet of rice paper in for about 15 seconds, until soft and flexible.
Lay the softened rice paper flat on a plate or board.
In the lower third, layer a little lettuce, rice vermicelli, carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, and mint.
Fold the bottom up over the filling, fold in the sides, and roll it up snugly like a small burrito.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Serve with the peanut sauce for dipping.

title: Baba Ganoush
summary: Smoky roasted eggplant whipped with tahini, lemon, and garlic into a silky dip. Scoop it up with warm pita or crisp vegetables.

steps.step: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Prick the eggplants all over with a fork and set them on a baking sheet.
Roast, turning once, until the skins are blistered and the insides are completely soft, about 35 minutes.
Let the eggplants cool, then scoop the soft flesh into a bowl and discard the skins.
Mash the eggplant with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, and salt until creamy but still a little chunky.
Spread onto a plate and drizzle with the olive oil.
Scatter the parsley over the top before serving.
